evidence: app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:72-79 — Abilities section links to /abilities/*, must be edited too or every Pokémon page links to 404s
app/shared/types/pokedex.ts:25-29 — AbilityData, Card.hidden and PokemonData.abilities need cleanup
app/app/components/CardList.vue:7 — hidden plumbing exists only for abilities and lingers as dead code if unswept
removability.rationale: Deleting the route is trivial, but the feature has tentacles into the Pokémon page's spec-mandated section, the shared types, and the Card.hidden plumbing — a handful of small, grep-findable edits rather than one delete.

evidence: app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:5-13 — sprite URL built in exactly one component; the Deoxys-class bug is fixed once and covers home, moves, abilities and types lists
app/app/components/MovesTable.vue:62-77 — all sortable tables share one sorting implementation
app/app/pages/index.vue:101-107 — card-grid markup duplicated instead of using CardList, so list-level changes land in two templates
app/app/error.vue:13-31 — app shell duplicated from app/app/app.vue; nav/footer changes must be made twice
changeability.rationale: The hardest bug class (per-card rendering) is genuinely one-place, and move-table logic is centralized; two structural duplications (home card grid, error.vue shell) mean several other changes land in two spots.

evidence: app/shared/types/pokedex.ts — pages consume typed view-models and never parse raw PokeAPI payloads; a real narrow seam
app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:5 — UI component knows the media path pattern and reads runtimeConfig directly, while artwork URLs come from the server (app/server/api/pokemon/[name].get.ts:30)
app/app/pages/index.vue:106 — re-implements the label fallback that exists as typeRef in app/server/utils/data.ts:62
app/server/api/pokemon/[name]/moves.get.ts:44 and app/app/components/MovesTable.vue:100 — row identity (name:level) encoded independently on both sides
coupling.rationale: Server and client are cleanly separated by the shared view-model types — the important seam. Remaining tangles are small: one client-side data-shape assumption, a fallback rule in two layers, a duplicated composite key.

evidence: app/app/components/PageSection.vue — title + slot with useId; stretches to every section on every page
app/app/components/MovesTable.vue:13 — showLevel boolean covers the one real variation without flag creep
app/app/components/CardList.vue:3-14 — takes plain Card[] but can't express the home page's per-card types, so app/app/pages/index.vue:101-107 inlined the grid
app/server/utils/pokeapi.ts:23-60 — fetchApi/fetchResource/fetchList/mapLimit are exactly the primitives an Items section would reuse
app/shared/utils/format.ts — humanize/display/dexNumber shared by every layer
abstraction_design.rationale: Components are designed around the app's actual variation and the data helpers would be reused wholesale for Items. The one miss is CardList not stretching to the home page's card variant, which produced copy-paste instead of a flag.

findings.issue: Sprite URL is constructed in the UI component from runtimeConfig plus a hard-coded media path, while artwork URLs arrive via the server payload; media-path knowledge lives client-side, split from the server's URL handling.
findings.suggestion: Include the sprite URL in the server view-model (as already done for artwork) so PokemonCard only renders what it's given.

findings.issue: Home page duplicates the card-grid list markup instead of using CardList, because CardList has no way to pass per-card types.
findings.suggestion: Extend CardList with optional card types (or a scoped slot / richer Card type) and use it here, so list-level changes land in one component.

findings.issue: The full app shell (banner, nav, footer) is copy-pasted from app.vue with plain <a> tags instead of NuxtLink; nav and footer edits must be made in two files.
findings.suggestion: Extract the shell into a layout (or shared component) and render <NuxtLayout> inside error.vue for a single source of truth.

findings.issue: Type-label fallback (`labels.get(name) ?? humanize(name)`) is re-implemented client-side although the identical rule exists as typeRef in server/utils/data.ts:62.
findings.suggestion: Move typeRef into shared/utils/format.ts, or have the server send labelled TypeRefs as other endpoints already do.

findings.issue: The Moves section hand-rolls the section/panel/aria-labelledby markup PageSection encapsulates, because PageSection cannot set a fragment id for #moves.
findings.suggestion: Give PageSection an optional id prop that overrides useId.

findings.issue: Row identity `${name}:${level}` is duplicated in app/server/api/pokemon/[name]/moves.get.ts:44 (dedupe key) and here (v-for key); changing one without the other silently breaks dedupe or keys.
findings.suggestion: Have the server emit a stable row id in MoveRow, or document the key contract next to both uses.

findings.issue: Card.hidden, CardList's hidden pass-through and PokemonCard's 'Hidden ability' note exist solely for the abilities feature; removing Abilities leaves dead code across three files.
findings.suggestion: When removing the feature, grep for `hidden` and remove the whole chain, or fold the note into a generic per-card badge mechanism.

findings.issue: The endpoint is named /api/species but returns the home-page index (species + type and generation filters); the name invites collision with a future species resource and misleads greps.
findings.suggestion: Rename to /api/index or /api/dex-index and update the single consumer (app/app/pages/index.vue:9).

summary: A well-factored Nuxt 4 app: Nitro handlers build typed view-models from shared/types, pages stay thin, and a small component set captures the app's real variation. Most edits — the sprite bug, move-table sorting, stats, caching — land in one obvious place. The main editability debts are the duplicated app shell in error.vue, the home page bypassing CardList, and client-side sprite-URL construction, each of which turns one change into two.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Two files delete cleanly, but the spec-mandated Abilities section on the Pokémon page links to them, and the hidden-ability plumbing spans the Card type, CardList and PokemonCard; all edits are small and grep-findable.

scenarios.change: Fix the wrong-sprite bug for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: Every list (home directly, moves/abilities/types via CardList) renders PokemonCard, so the single sprite-URL computed at PokemonCard.vue:5 covers everything.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: Server lists are ordered inside speciesCards (data.ts:81) and the home page has its own inline grid; you either sort in CardList plus index.vue separately, or thread a sort option through speciesCards and its three handler call sites — the CardList/index.vue duplication is what costs the second edit.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: Data helpers (fetchResource, fetchList, englishName, shortEffect) and UI components (PageSection, CardList, TypeBadge, NotFound) reuse as-is; the ~40-line moves page is copied with swapped fields, there is no existing list-page template for /items, and the nav lives in both app.vue and error.vue.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Base URL is defined once in runtimeConfig and read by pokeapi.ts; caching (TTL, cache map) lives only in pokeapi.ts:7-19. The one wrinkle is PokemonCard.vue:5, which independently reads apiBase and hard-codes the media path.
